data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject only if the test's failure can be distinguished from the subject's failure; when the installation protocol conflates the two, as in shown-to-fail-first, the test describes the conflation rather than constraining either side.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the 1/9 mutation were detectable by a different test that does not rely on the distinction","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 3-of-26 result included mutations that attack the subject's behavior directly","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the distinction were re-established by an independent check not shown in the record","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The 1/9 loss in compile.py is the case where the mutation removes the distinction between test-failure and subject-failure, because the mutation is in the code that performs the distinction. The other modules preserve the distinction because their guards are not the code that performs the distinction. The 3-of-26 result is the count of mutations that attack the distinction itself rather than the subject's behavior.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
